key_insight: The paper shows that the token unmasking order in masked diffusion language models is not just a decoding detail but a learnable "order of thought" that can be optimized to improve generation quality.
engineering_relevance: For practical AI systems, Self-Aware Scheduling offers a lightweight way to boost diffusion-model decoding without changing the frozen denoiser, making schedule design a trainable control knob for reasoning and generation.
method: Derives an upper bound on sequential decoding mismatch using KL divergence and pathwise log-likelihood.
Turns order selection into policy optimization with a dense self-aware reward over ordered trajectories.
Trains a lightweight order policy with Group Relative Policy Optimization and applies it to any-order and semi-autoregressive decoding.
evidence_signal: Across tasks, SAS improved Sudoku accuracy from 82.0% to 91.8% with a 1B model and raised GSM8K pass@1 from 64% to 76% and MBPP from 39.5% to 41% with LLaDA-8B.
watch_item: The learned schedule depends on policy optimization and may require careful tuning, and its gains are reported on specific benchmark settings that may not transfer uniformly to all diffusion LMs or decoding regimes.
paper_title: Scheduling Thoughts: Learning the Order of Thought in Diffusion Language Models
